cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android_payload/scripts/NameGenerator.as:145-166 + QuestEngine.as:522-526 + reference/extracted/bindata/98_1t4653s0.bin
lane_impact: L-world-map: refutes bindata/place-name-26x26-lookup's 'recovered whole'. The correct generator is the 78x37 compound, giving 2,886 possible names, deterministic per territory.
quote: NameGenerator.as:147-153 `var namex:int = territoryx % 137; var namey:int = territoryy % 26; if(namex < 26) { return this.getTownName1(namex,namey); } return this.getTownName2(territoryID);` ; :162-165 `public function getTownName2(territoryID:int) : String { var rng:RNG = new RNG(territoryID * 2); return this.namestarting[rng.rand(this.namestarting.length)] + this.nameending[rng.rand(this.nameending.length)]; }` — I counted the arrays: namestarting = 78, nameending = 37. Measured over all 735 land territories: territoryx in [329,389], namex in [55,115], getTownName1 hit count = 0/735.
text: bindata/98's 677 place names are DORMANT in the shipped world. getPlaceName gates the 26x26 lookup on `namex = territoryx % 137` being < 26, but every real territory's raw x lies in [329,389] (from the bitmap transform), so namex is always in [55,115]. getTownName1 is reached for ZERO of the 735 land territories. Every shipped place name is either a hardcoded exception or a getTownName2 compound: namestarting[78] concatenated with nameending[37], seeded RNG(territoryID*2). Anyone porting world naming from the 677-entry table will produce names the original never generated.

cite: reference/decompiled/shs3_android_payload/scripts/MCSPlayer.as:3019-3095, :107, :222 + StatsManager.as:1905-1919 + EnemyPlayer.as:757 + InputManager.as:51,106-108,198 + reference/decompiled/shs3_payload/scripts/§1t1523s0§.as:2347
lane_impact: L-combat-model: directly refutes bindata/reach-cap-not-in-this-source and closes the ledger's single named blocker. Web-verified, so the S0 build-parity caveat does not apply.
ledger_text: | **combat-model** | reach cap | the single per-stance value the whole combat model needs — MISSING |
quote: MCSPlayer.as:3030 `this.slashLength = this.baseSlashLength * 1.5;` · :3041 `this.slashLength = this.baseSlashLength * (1 + 0.5 * this.balancedMastery * 0.01);` · :3052-3055 `this.slashLength = this.baseSlashLength * (0.5 + 0.5 * this.heavyMastery * 0.01); if(this.slashLength < 100) { this.slashLength = 100; }` · :3078-3081 DUAL `this.slashLength = this.baseSlashLength;` floor 100 · :3094 `InputManager.setMaxDistance(this.slashLength);` ; StatsManager.as:1915-1918 `internal static function getBaseSlashLengthVal(speed:int) : int { var maxincrement:int = 90 + getPlayerStats(STAT_DAN) * 5; return int(120 + Math.floor(maxincrement * speed / (20 + speed))); }` ; EnemyPlayer.as:757 `var baseSlashLength:int = 120 + Math.floor(maxincrement * val / (20 + val));` ; InputManager.as:51 `internal static var maxDistance:int = 200;` ; WEB §1t1523s0§.as:2347 `return int(120 + Math.floor(_loc2_ * param1 / (20 + param1)));`
text: THE PER-STANCE REACH CAP IN STAGE PIXELS IS RECOVERED IN FULL. MCSPlayer.setStance sets it per stance and feeds it straight to the input line: LIGHT = baseSlashLength*1.5; BALANCED = baseSlashLength*(1 + 0.5*balancedMastery*0.01); HEAVY = baseSlashLength*(0.5 + 0.5*heavyMastery*0.01) with a hard floor of 100; REVERSED = *1.5; DUAL = base with floor 100; then InputManager.setMaxDistance(slashLength). The base is 120 + floor((90 + STAT_DAN*5) * speed / (20 + speed)), speed = STAT_SPEED + bonus, x1.5 under BUFF_SPEED, halved by BUFF_INJURED. AI opponents use the same shape with maxincrement fixed at 90. Default before any stance is set is 200. So reach IS the stance trade-off: light reaches 1.5x, heavy only 0.5x at zero mastery and reaches parity only at 100% heavy mastery.
